content.title: About
content.content: The Light Ice Cream Sandwich is made of two delicate wafer cookies filled with a layer of chocolate ice cream. The product has lower calories than traditional ice cream sandwiches thanks to a light cream base and reduced sugar content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate ice cream sandwich appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
The light version was developed in the 2010s to cut calories without sacrificing taste.
It uses natural cocoa powder instead of artificial flavorings.
Each sandwich is individually wrapped in an aluminum film to preserve freshness.
The product is often used in culinary workshops as a base for dessert decorations.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: The light formula provides about 150 kcal per serving, allowing it to fit into a balanced diet.

items.title: Source of Calcium
items.content: The dairy base supplies roughly 10 % of the daily calcium requirement, supporting bone health.

items.title: Contains Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa powder is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy Support
items.content: A modest amount of carbohydrates offers a quick source of energy after workouts.

items.title: Reduced Sugar
items.content: Lower sugar levels make the product more suitable for those monitoring glycemic impact.

items.title: Milk Protein Allergy
items.content: The product contains milk and may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Gluten Content
items.content: The wafers contain wheat, so it is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Storage at High Temperatures
items.content: Prolonged storage at room temperature can cause the ice cream to melt, affecting texture and flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Keep the sandwich frozen and serve immediately after removal. It can be halved and topped with berries, nuts, or grated chocolate for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the freezer at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, consume within 2‑3 days and avoid refreezing.
